claims.text: Large language models are systematically overconfident when constructing confidence intervals around their answers.
Across several modern LLMs, nominal 99% confidence intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average on Fermi-style estimation questions.
Adjusting LLM confidence intervals with a conformal prediction based approach yields accurate 99% observed coverage.
Adjusting LLM confidence intervals with a conformal prediction based approach decreases the Winkler interval score by 54%.
Direct log-probability elicitation reduces overconfidence at high confidence levels.
Quantile adjustment methods reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.
Under perception-tunnel theory, LLMs exhibit overconfidence because they act as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution, neglecting its tails.

evidence.description: We study how well LLMs construct confidence intervals around their own answers and find that they are systematically overconfident.
Across several modern models, nominal 99% intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
With a conformal prediction based approach that adjusts the intervals, we obtain accurate 99% observed coverage.
With a conformal prediction based approach that adjusts the intervals... the Winkler interval score decreases by 54%.
We also propose direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment methods, which further reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.

Finally, we develop a perception-tunnel theory explaining why LLMs exhibit overconfidence: when reasoning under uncertainty, they act as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution, neglecting its tails.

methodologies.name: FermiEval
methodologies.description: A benchmark of Fermi-style estimation questions with a scoring rule for confidence interval coverage and sharpness.

methodologies.name: Conformal prediction interval adjustment
methodologies.description: A conformal prediction approach that adjusts confidence intervals to improve empirical coverage and lower Winkler interval scores.

methodologies.name: Direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment
methodologies.description: Elicitation and adjustment techniques designed to reduce LLM overconfidence at high confidence levels.

limitations.text: Large language models struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty and produce severely miscalibrated confidence intervals (nominal 99% intervals cover true answers only 65% of the time).
